text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: unusual auth fail spike for auth-service in us-west-2. 1200 failures/min, elevated 5xx on token-validate endpoint. Auto-escalation -> oncall@sre.
sam: oncall here — looking. grabbing logs and will check recent deploys.
maria: I see a pattern: many failures originate from a tight set of IPs hitting /v1/auth/validate with malformed tokens. Possible replay/fuzzing. I can dump a sample.
tilIy: copying query, running quick aggregation. looks like 3 IP prefixes account for ~73% of requests. also seeing repeated `X-Request-Id` values (probing).
security-bot: Rule hit: "suspicious-auth-probe" threshold crossed. Created incident ticket INC-2026-4372. Notifying security on-call.
ops: can we temporarily block those prefixes at the edge? nginx rate-limits are saturated. recommend network-level drop and token introspection rate cap.
sam: agreed. applying abrupt drop rule in cloud firewall for the three prefixes. patching in 1m rule. command: ```
# block prefixes
cloud-fw block 203.0.113.0/24
cloud-fw block 198.51.100.0/24
cloud-fw block 192.0.2.0/25
```
maria: started a quick grep for potential leaked tokens in logs; found ~14 occurrences of clear-text tokens in debug logs pushed to staging S3 prefix last night. Possibly misconfigured debug level on auth-service job.
tilly: if tokens leaked to S3 we need immediate rotation and customer impact assessment. list of affected service accounts?
security-bot: preliminary risk: low-medium until we confirm whether tokens are live keys or ephemeral session tokens. Marking as P1 until rotation complete.
ops: can we rotate consumer-facing client secrets first? which keys to rotate without causing mass user disruption?
sam: plan: (1) block offending IPs (done), (2) throttle token introspection, (3) revoke and rotate service keys that had clear-text exposure, (4) invalidate active session tokens older than 24h for the affected scope, (5) notify customers if we confirm exfil. executing steps 1-2 now.
maria: listing exposed artifacts: s3://redwood-logs-staging/auth/debug/YYYY-MM-DD/*.log — looks like a scheduled debug job wrote there between 03:12-03:24 UTC. Affected keys belong to two internal service accounts and one customer-integrated client id.
support-lead: hold on customer notifications until we confirm the customer-integrated client id is actually live keys; I'll prep a templated advisory and hold for OK.
security-bot: create rotation tasks: TASK-rotate-kms-keys, TASK-revoke-service-tokens, TASK-audit-s3-access. Assigning to ops and sec-team.
ops: starting rotation for two internal service accounts (non-customer facing). Running command: ```
# rotate service account keys
sactl rotate --id sa-auth-worker-1
sactl rotate --id sa-auth-worker-2
```
sam: revocation in progress for sessions with scope `auth:validate:prod` older than 24h. Running batch invalidate: ```
sessionctl invalidate --scope auth:validate:prod --older-than 24h --dry-run
sessionctl invalidate --scope auth:validate:prod --older-than 24h --confirm
```
maria: confirming the customer-integrated client id looks like a test integration; reached out to account owner `@acct-jensen` via DM. No public commits found with that token but we need to be cautious.
tilIy: small typo: (tilly) -> correcting: we should also snapshot the logs and set retention to prevent accidental further exposure. backing up the s3 prefix and locking ACLs now.
ops: ACLs set to private, bucket policy pinned, temp credentials invalidated for debug job.
security-bot: recommended immediate key rotation for any key appearing in logs. If customer key affected, escalate to legal/PR.
sam: rotation completed for internal keys. Please confirm session revokes succeeded and monitor auth error rates.
maria: grep completed. after rotation, no new occurrences of those tokens in logs. scanning for exfil patterns to external buckets — none found so far.
support-lead: preparing customer advisory draft (internal review). tagging it as "possible token exposure; investigation ongoing; rotation done; investigating customer impact".
tilly: monitoring dashboards — token-validate 5xx returned to baseline after firewall block + throttles. latency slightly higher for short window but stabilizing.
security-bot: Incident update: containment achieved. Next actions: full audit of debug-job config, enforce deploy-time lint to disallow debug-level logging in prod, add S3 write guard (block public/unsafe prefixes), and run credential scan on commit history for related repos.
sam: passing to next oncall: @tilly please own the follow-ups and run the post-incident checklist. I'll update the ticket with steps taken and close once follow-ups verified.
tilly: ack. I'll schedule a short war-room tomorrow 16:00 UTC with sec/ops/dev to review root cause and mitigations.
support-lead: will wait for final confirmation before outbound customer comms.
security-bot: closing P1 status to "contained". Will remain open for post-incident actions. :white_check_mark:
